newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends down on BOK's dlr buying-dealers.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends down on BOK's dlr buying-dealers.

text.p: The won closed lower against the dollar on Tuesday due to what dealers said was the central bank's dollar buying in forward trading.
The won ended at 893.00 against Monday's closing and today's opening of 892.50. It moved between 890.60 and 893.40.
"The Bank of Korea appears to have bought about $100 million in one-month forward trading," said a domestic bank dealer.
Dealers said the planned expansion of the foreign stockholding limit on May 2 depressed buying of dollars in early trading.
There were some dollar supplies from exporters and companies which had to pay taxes and salaries.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 892.10/30 on Wednesday, compared with 892.70 today.
The finance ministry said the stock holding limit would be expanded to 23 percent from the current 20 percent.
A foreign bank dealer forecast a range of 891.00 to 894.00 on Wednesday, while the domestic bank dealer put it between 892.00 and 894.00.
